Subpart E—Capital and Operational Backstop
§ 15.40
Capital.
(a)
Capital.
The total of a permitted payment stablecoin issuer's equity accounts, as determined under U.S. GAAP, less deductions specified in paragraph (b) of this section, must meet or exceed the minimum capital requirement in § 15.41(a).
(b)
Capital deductions
—(1)
Intangible assets and deferred tax assets.
(i) Goodwill;
(ii) Any other intangible asset as determined under U.S. GAAP; and
(iii) Deferred tax assets, net of valuation allowances.
(2)
Operational backstop assets funded by equity.
The total operational backstop assets required under § 15.41(b), less the amount of operational backstop debt as defined in paragraph (c) of this section.
(c)
Operational backstop debt.
Operational backstop debt consists of debt instruments in an amount that in total does not exceed 50 percent of the operational backstop requirement in § 15.41(b) and where each debt instrument:
(1) Is issued and paid in;
(2) Is subordinated to the claims of payment stablecoin holders and general creditors of the permitted payment stablecoin issuer;
(3) Is unsecured, including not being backed by the establishment of any fund for payment prior to maturity, covered by a guarantee, or subject to any other arrangement that legally or economically enhances the seniority of the instrument;
(4) Has a minimum maturity date of at least five years. At the beginning of each of the last five years of the life of the instrument, the maximum amount of the instrument that is eligible to be included as operational backstop debt decreases by 20 percent per year of the otherwise full qualifying amount, and the instrument is excluded from operational backstop debt completely when the remaining maturity is less than one year;
(5) May be callable by its terms only after a minimum of five years after issuance and only with the prior written approval of the OCC. In addition, the permitted payment stablecoin issuer must either replace the instrument to be called with an equivalent amount of a new instrument meeting the criteria for operational backstop debt or demonstrate in writing to the OCC that the permitted payment stablecoin issuer has sufficient capital to meet its minimum capital requirement in § 15.41;
(6) Allows for scheduled repayment of principal only at maturity and does not allow for the acceleration of any principal or interest payment, except in the event of the receivership, insolvency, liquidation, or similar proceeding, as applicable, of the permitted payment stablecoin issuer;
(7) Does not have a credit-sensitive feature, but may include a variable interest rate based on prevalent market interest rates;
(8) Does not prohibit the permitted payment stablecoin issuer from issuing other capital or debt instruments; and
(9) Is not funded, directly or indirectly, by any affiliate of the permitted payment stablecoin issuer.
§ 15.41
Minimum capital and operational backstop.
(a)
Minimum
c
apital requirement.
A permitted payment stablecoin issuer must hold minimum capital as follows:
(1)
De novo capital requirement.
(i) A de novo permitted payment stablecoin issuer must hold minimum capital equal to the greater of:
(A) The amount specified as part of its OCC licensing or chartering conditions; or
(B) $5 million.
(ii) A de novo permitted payment stablecoin issuer means a permitted payment stablecoin issuer that has received OCC approval to issue a payment stablecoin under this part within the prior 3 years or a State qualified payment stablecoin issuer that has transitioned to the Federal regulatory framework under this part within the prior 3 years and has not received a waiver under § 15.15(d).
(iii) A de novo permitted payment stablecoin issuer must hold this minimum amount for 36 months, or for a shorter or longer period as specified as part of its chartering conditions or as subsequently determined by the OCC based on the experience of the permitted payment stablecoin issuer.
(2)
Ongoing capital requirement.
(i) A permitted payment stablecoin issuer must maintain capital commensurate with the level and nature of all risks to which the permitted payment stablecoin issuer is exposed, including risks for off-balance-sheet activities.
(ii) A permitted payment stablecoin issuer must have a process for assessing its overall capital adequacy in relation to its business model and risk profile and a comprehensive strategy for sustaining an appropriate level of capital to maintain ongoing operations.
(iii) A permitted payment stablecoin issuer must hold minimum capital of no less than $5 million.
(b)
Operational backstop requirement.
A permitted payment stablecoin issuer must maintain assets:
(1) Equal to 12 months of total expenses.
(i) In the case of a permitted payment stablecoin issuer that has provided quarterly reports under § 15.14 for one year or more, the permitted payment stablecoin issuer must calculate the amount required under this paragraph (b)(1) using the quarterly expenses reported in the current quarterly report and the three immediately preceding reports.
(ii) For each calendar quarter in the preceding 12 months for which the permitted payment stablecoin issuer has not filed a quarterly report required under § 15.14, the permitted payment stablecoin issuer must calculate its expenses using:
(A) Actual expenses, in the case of a permitted payment stablecoin issuer that was in operation during a calendar quarter in which it did not file a quarterly report under § 15.14; or
(B) Reasonably determined expenses, which may include annualizing expenses from other quarters, in the case of any other permitted payment stablecoin issuer.
(iii) A permitted payment stablecoin issuer may exclude one-time expenses that are wholly unrelated to the
(
printed page 67193)
continuing operation of the permitted payment stablecoin issuer from the calculation under paragraph (b)(1)(i) or (ii) of this section with prior written approval of the OCC.
(iv) If a permitted payment stablecoin issuer acquires another permitted payment stablecoin issuer, the historical expenses of the acquired permitted payment stablecoin issuer must be added to the historical expenses of the acquiring permitted payment stablecoin issuer.
(2) Consisting of:
(i) United States coins and currency (including Federal Reserve notes) or money standing to the credit of an account with a Federal Reserve Bank;
(ii) Demand deposits or funds in share accounts that are payable on demand at a U.S. insured depository institution, the balances of which are fully insured by the FDIC or the National Credit Union Administration; and
(iii) U.S. Treasury bills, notes, or bonds with a remaining maturity of 93 days or less, or issued with a maturity of 93 days or less; and
(3) Separately identified from any reserve assets required under § 15.11 or other assets of the permitted payment stablecoin issuer on the reports filed under § 15.14.
(c)
Failure to meet minimum capital or backstop requirements.
(1) A permitted payment stablecoin issuer must comply with its minimum capital and backstop requirements at all times.
(i) A permitted payment stablecoin issuer must notify the OCC within 24 hours if it fails to meet either the minimum capital or backstop requirement during a quarter.
(ii) A permitted payment stablecoin issuer must publicly report whether it has complied with the minimum capital and backstop requirements during the quarter on the report required under § 15.14(i).
(2) A permitted payment stablecoin issuer that fails to satisfy its minimum capital or backstop requirement during a quarter and remains noncompliant at the end of the quarter is prohibited from issuing any new payment stablecoins starting on the first day of the following month and until such time as it satisfies its minimum capital and backstop requirements, except as necessary to facilitate a transfer of payment stablecoins from one distributed ledger to another and provided that the net outstanding issuance value does not increase.
(3) If a permitted payment stablecoin issuer fails to meet its minimum capital or backstop requirements at the end of two consecutive quarters, it must:
(i) Begin liquidation of reserve assets and redemption of outstanding payment stablecoins, consistent with § 15.12;
(ii) Not charge customers a fee to redeem their payment stablecoins; and
(iii) Not issue any new payment stablecoins going forward.
(4) After notification to the OCC under paragraph (c)(1)(i) of this section, the OCC may impose the restrictions described in paragraph (c)(2) of this section prior to the end of the quarter if it does not appear that the permitted payment stablecoin issuer will regain compliance with the minimum capital or operational backstop requirements, or as otherwise may be necessary for the protection of payment stablecoin holders.
(5) Notwithstanding paragraphs (c)(2) and (c)(3) of this section, the OCC may permit a permitted payment stablecoin issuer to continue operations while its operational backstop is below the required amount if the backstop assets were liquidated to address a temporary disruption or other operational event, the permitted payment stablecoin issuer provides a plan within seven days to regain compliance with the operational backstop requirement within 90 days, and the OCC deems the plan viable.
(d)
Uninsured national trust bank minimum capital requirement.
(1) An uninsured national trust bank, whether or not it is a permitted payment stablecoin issuer, may elect to comply with all of the requirements in §§ 15.40 through 15.42 in lieu of complying with the requirements in
12 CFR part 3
upon receipt of the OCC's prior approval.
(2) To make the election described in paragraph (d)(1) of this section, an uninsured national trust bank must submit a written request for prior approval to the appropriate OCC supervisory office, along with documentation sufficient to support the bank's minimum capital and operational backstop amounts.
(3) The OCC will approve or deny the request within 60 days after OCC receipt of a complete request.
(4) An uninsured national trust bank may rescind an approved election under this paragraph (d) by submitting a notice to the appropriate OCC supervisory office. The rescission is effective upon receipt by the OCC.
(5) Notwithstanding paragraph (d)(1) of this section, an uninsured national trust bank must comply with any OCC enforcement action, order, directive, or document that specifies a different minimum capital requirement that applies to the national trust bank.
§ 15.42
Individual additional capital or operational backstop requirement.
(a)
Applicability.
The OCC may require an additional capital or backstop requirement for a permitted payment stablecoin issuer if appropriate under the particular facts and circumstances. For example, an additional capital or backstop requirement may be appropriate for:
(1) Failure of management to assess an appropriate capital requirement to support ongoing operations consistent with the permitted payment stablecoin issuer's business model and risk profile;
(2) A permitted payment stablecoin issuer that has, or is expected to have, losses resulting in capital inadequacy;
(3) A permitted payment stablecoin issuer with significant exposure due to management's overall inability to monitor and control financial and operating risks;
(4) A permitted payment stablecoin issuer that is experiencing significant volatility in payment stablecoin issuance or redemption;
(5) A permitted payment stablecoin issuer with significant exposure due to fiduciary or operational risk;
(6) A permitted payment stablecoin issuer's significant off-balance-sheet activities; or
(7) A permitted payment stablecoin issuer that may be adversely affected by the activities or condition of its affiliate(s), or other persons or institutions with which it has significant business relationships.
(b)
Standards for determination.
The factors to be considered in the determination will vary in each case and may include, for example:
(1) The conditions or circumstances leading to the OCC's determination that an additional capital or backstop requirement is appropriate or necessary for the permitted payment stablecoin issuer;
(2) The exigency of those circumstances or potential problems;
(3) The overall condition, management strength, and future prospects of the permitted payment stablecoin issuer and, if applicable, its affiliate(s);
(4) The permitted payment stablecoin issuer's liquidity, capital, and stablecoin reserve assets compared to its peer group; and
(5) The views of the permitted payment stablecoin issuer's owners and senior management in any response provided under paragraph (c)(2) of this section.
(c)
Procedures—
(1)
Notice.
When the OCC determines that an additional capital or backstop requirement above that set forth in § 15.41 is necessary or
(
printed page 67194)
appropriate for a particular permitted payment stablecoin issuer, the OCC will notify the permitted payment stablecoin issuer in writing of the proposed additional capital or backstop requirement and the date by which the requirement should be reached (if applicable) and will provide an explanation of why the requirement proposed is considered necessary or appropriate for the permitted payment stablecoin issuer.
(2)
Response.
(i)(A) The permitted payment stablecoin issuer may respond to the OCC in writing to the notice.
(B) The response should include any matters that the permitted payment stablecoin issuer requests that the OCC consider in deciding whether an individual additional capital or backstop requirement should be established for the permitted payment stablecoin issuer, what the capital or backstop requirement should be, and, if applicable, when it should be achieved.
(C) Any response must be delivered to the OCC within 30 days after the date on which the permitted payment stablecoin issuer received the notice or such other time period as the OCC determines appropriate based on the condition of the permitted payment stablecoin issuer.
(ii) Failure to respond within the time period specified by the OCC in the notice constitutes a waiver of any objections to the proposed individual additional capital or backstop requirement or the deadline for its achievement.
(3)
Decision.
(i) After the close of the permitted payment stablecoin issuer's response period, the OCC will decide, based on a review of the permitted payment stablecoin issuer's response and other information concerning the permitted payment stablecoin issuer, whether the individual additional capital or backstop requirement should be established for the permitted payment stablecoin issuer and, if so, the requirement and the date the requirement will become effective.
(ii) The permitted payment stablecoin issuer will be notified of the decision in writing.
(iii) The notice will include an explanation of the decision, except for a decision not to establish an individual additional capital or backstop requirement for the permitted payment stablecoin issuer.
(4)
Submission of plan.
The decision in paragraph (c)(3) of this section may require the permitted payment stablecoin issuer to develop and submit to the OCC, within a time period specified, an acceptable plan to reach the additional capital or backstop requirement established for the permitted payment stablecoin issuer by the date required.
(5)
Change in circumstances.
If, after the OCC's decision in paragraph (c)(3) of this section, there is a significant change in the circumstances that materially affects the permitted payment stablecoin issuer's capital adequacy or its ability to reach the required additional capital or backstop requirement by the specified date, the permitted payment stablecoin issuer may request a change in the additional capital or backstop requirement for the permitted payment stablecoin issuer, the date when the minimum must be achieved, or the permitted payment stablecoin issuer's plan (if applicable). Pending a decision on reconsideration, the OCC's original decision and any plan required under that decision continue in full force and effect.

Department of the Treasury
Office of the Comptroller of the Currency
AGENCY:
Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), Treasury.
ACTION:
Notice and request for comment.
SUMMARY:
The OCC, as part of its continuing effort to reduce paperwork and respondent burden, invites comment on a new information collection, as required by the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 (PRA). In accordance with the requirements of the PRA, the OCC may not conduct or sponsor, and the respondent is not required to respond to an information collection unless it displays a currently valid Office of Management and Budget (OMB) control number. The OCC is proposing a new information collection titled “Reporting Forms and Instructions for Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuers Subject to the Jurisdiction of the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency,” that would include weekly and quarterly reporting forms that must be completed by permitted payment stablecoin issuers and foreign payment stablecoin issuers. The OCC is seeking a new OMB control number for this information collection. The OCC also is giving notice that it has sent the collection to OMB for review.
DATES:
Comments must be received by November 23, 2026.
ADDRESSES:
Commenters are encouraged to submit comments by email, if possible. You may submit comments by any of the following methods:
Email:
prainfo@occ.treas.gov
.
Mail:
Chief Counsel's Office, Attention: Comment Processing, Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, Attention: 1557-NEW, 400 7th Street SW, Suite 1E-216, Washington, DC 20219.
Hand Delivery/Courier:
400 7th Street SW, Suite 1E-216, Washington, DC 20219.
Fax:
(571) 293-4835.
Instructions:
You must include “OCC” as the agency name and “1557-NEW” in your comment. In general, the OCC will publish comments on
www.reginfo.gov
without change, including any business or personal information provided, such as name and address information, email addresses, or phone numbers. Comments received, including attachments and other supporting materials, are part of the public record and subject to public disclosure. Do not include any information in your comment or supporting materials that you consider confidential or inappropriate for public disclosure.
Written comments and recommendations for the proposed information collection should also be sent within 30 days of publication of this notice to
www.reginfo.gov/​public/​do/​PRAMain
.
You can find this information collection by selecting “Currently under 30-day Review—Open for Public Comments” or by using the search function.
You may review comments and other related materials that pertain to this information collection following the close of the 30-day comment period for this notice by the method set forth in the next bullet.
Viewing Comments Electronically:
Go to
www.reginfo.gov
.
Hover over the “Information Collection Review” tab and click on “Information Collection Review” from the drop-down menu. From the “Currently under Review” drop-down menu, select “Department of the Treasury” and then click “submit.” This information collection can be located by searching OMB control number “1557-NEW” or “Reporting Forms and Instructions for Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuers Subject to the Jurisdiction of the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.” Upon finding the appropriate information collection, click on the related “ICR Reference Number.” On the next screen, select “View Supporting Statement and Other Documents” and then click on the link to any comment listed at the bottom of the screen.
For assistance in navigating
www.reginfo.gov
,
please contact the Regulatory Information Service Center at (202) 482-7340.
FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT:
Shaquita Merritt, Clearance Officer, (202) 649-5490, Chief Counsel's Office, Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, 400 7th Street SW, Washington, DC 20219. If you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech disability, please dial 7-1-1 to access telecommunications relay services.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION:
Under the PRA (
44 U.S.C. 3501
et seq.
), Federal agencies must obtain approval from the OMB for each collection of information that they conduct or sponsor. “Collection of information” is defined in
44 U.S.C. 3502(3)
and
5 CFR 1320.3(c)
to include agency requests or requirements that members of the public submit reports, keep records, or provide information to a third party. The OCC asks the OMB to approve the collection in this notice.
Title:
Reporting Forms and Instructions for Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuers Subject to the Jurisdiction of the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency.
OMB Control No.:
1557-NEW.
Type of Review:
Regular.
Affected Public:
Businesses or other for-profit.
Description:
The Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act (
12 U.S.C. 5901
et seq.
) (GENIUS Act or the Act) was enacted on July 18, 2025. The GENIUS Act establishes a regulatory framework for payment stablecoin activities. On March 2, 2026, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) issued a proposed rule that would implement requirements of the Act with respect to the issuance of payment stablecoins and certain related activities by entities subject to the OCC's jurisdiction (the proposed rule).
[
1
]
On
(
printed page 66917)
June 12, 2026, the OCC proposed weekly and quarterly reporting forms (Form PS-01 and Form PS-02, respectively) that permitted payment stablecoin issuers and foreign payment stablecoin issuers subject to the OCC's jurisdiction would be required to file with the OCC.
[
2
]
The OCC issued a final rule implementing the requirements of the GENIUS Act with respect to the issuance of payment stablecoins and certain related activities by entities subject to the OCC's jurisdiction (the final rule), published elsewhere in this issue of the
Federal Register
.
[
3
]
These reporting forms would help ensure compliance with the final rule, facilitate OCC supervision of permitted payment stablecoin issuers and foreign payment stablecoin issuers, and would promote transparency with respect to the financial condition of permitted payment stablecoin issuers and foreign payment stablecoin issuers. Twelve CFR 15.14 of the final rule requires a permitted payment stablecoin issuer to submit two reports to the OCC. Section 15.14(h) requires a permitted payment stablecoin issuer to submit a weekly confidential reporting form to the OCC for each payment stablecoin it issues, and section 15.14(i) requires a permitted payment stablecoin issuer to submit a quarterly reporting form to the OCC. Section 15.31(b)(2) of the final rule requires a foreign payment stablecoin issuer registered with the OCC to produce the reports required of a permitted payment stablecoin issuer under section 15.14. With this issuance, the OCC is publishing a revised set of the required weekly and quarterly reporting forms for public comment. The revised reporting forms, and their instructions, are available at
www.occ.gov
.
The proposed forms are published as text documents. However, the OCC expects to use eXtensible Markup Language (commonly known as “XML”) or another format for permitted payment stablecoin issuers to submit reported data to enhance usability of the data. The final rule will be effective on January 18, 2027. This information collection would take effect as of the January 25, 2027, report date for OCC Reporting Form PS-01, Payment Stablecoin Activity and Reserve Weekly Reporting, and the March 31, 2027, report date for OCC Reporting Form PS-02, Permitted Payment Stablecoin Issuer and Foreign Payment Stablecoin Issuer Reports of Condition and Income.
Comments:
On June 12, 2026, the OCC published a 60-day notice for this proposed information collection.
[
4
]
The agency received several public comments for the agency's consideration.
General Comments Regarding Forms PS-01 and PS-02
On June 12, 2026, the OCC proposed a weekly reporting form, Form PS-01, and a quarterly reporting form, Form PS-02, that permitted payment stablecoin issuers and foreign payment stablecoin issuers, subject to the OCC's jurisdiction, would be required to file with the OCC. The notice accompanying the forms invited comment on Forms PS-01 and PS-02 generally as well as certain technical aspects of the forms. The comment period closed on August 11, 2026, and the OCC received approximately 20 comments in total. The comments focused on numerous aspects of the proposed forms as well as the overall reporting framework. Below is a discussion of the comments the OCC received concerning the overall reporting framework and technical comments that apply to both Form PS-01 and Form PS-02. Comments specific to Form PS-01 and Form PS-02 are discussed below.
One commenter expressed support for a reporting framework that is targeted, risk-based, and aligned with the GENIUS Act and encouraged the OCC to tailor the reporting obligations to capture information most important to assessing compliance with the GENIUS Act's core requirements, while avoiding imposing duplicative or impracticable obligations. In response to this feedback, the OCC has revised the reporting forms to minimize duplication, reduce the overall reporting, and ensure that the information being collected from permitted payment stablecoin issuers and foreign payment stablecoin issuers is essential to the supervision of those entities. Upon implementation, the OCC will continue to assess the reporting forms to ensure that the data being reported serves a justifiable supervisory purpose and provides the OCC with information relevant to the supervision of permitted payment stablecoin issuers and foreign payment stablecoin issuers.
Several commenters expressed support for the issuance of a reporting framework jointly adopted by the primary Federal payment stablecoin regulators. Proposed Weekly Reporting Form PS-01
The proposed weekly reporting forms would, among other things, help ensure compliance with the reserve asset requirements in proposed sections 15.11 and 15.31(a)(3). Proposed Schedule A would collect information on top stablecoin holders and transactors and counterparty concentration information. Proposed Schedule B would collect information on day-over-day changes in outstanding payment stablecoins and information redemptions. Proposed Schedule C would collect information about a permitted payment stablecoin issuer's aggregate composition of reserve assets for each payment stablecoin it issues. Proposed Schedules D, E, F, G, and H would collect disaggregated information about specific classes of reserve assets (
e.g.,
U.S. Treasury securities on proposed Schedule E). Permitted payment stablecoin issuers and foreign payment stablecoin issuers would only be required to report information regarding reserve assets held pursuant to the GENIUS Act on Proposed Schedules C, D, E, F, G, and H. Permitted payment stablecoin issuers and foreign payment stablecoin issuers are not required to report information on these schedules regarding assets they own that are not held as reserve assets or transactions in which they have engaged unrelated to the maintenance of reserve assets. For example, permitted payment stablecoin issuers and foreign payment stablecoin issuers should not report U.S. Treasury securities they own on Schedule E if those U.S. Treasury securities do not comprise the reserve assets used to back outstanding stablecoin issuance pursuant to the GENIUS Act.
As a part of the notice, the OCC invited comments on what items should be modified or removed and whether any items should be added. The OCC received feedback on numerous aspects of proposed Form PS-01.
One commenter expressed support for the collection and stated that the weekly reporting asks for the right information at the right cadence, and the schedule structure introduced in the proposed rulemaking is sensible. Another commenter stated that the proposed schedules collect information that is both available to permitted payment stablecoin issuers and is relevant to the oversight of permitted payment stablecoin issuers. In contrast, another commenter stated that the proposed weekly reporting cadence has no identified analogue in the ordinary prudential reporting the OCC requires of a national bank in sound condition. The commenter also questioned why the Call Report and the monthly, independently examined reserve report leave a supervisory gap requiring a universal weekly filing. The commenter also expressed support for adopting monthly reporting instead of a weekly reporting cadence.
The OCC believes that requiring a permitted payment stablecoin issuer to provide a weekly confidential set of data for each payment stablecoin it issues will allow the agency to understand the permitted payment stablecoin issuer's operations and the risks unique to its business model. Monthly and quarterly reports do not provide a frequent enough reporting cadence to oversee risks and changes, given the short maturity of permitted payment stablecoin issuers' reserve assets. This regular data reporting will also allow the OCC to tailor its examinations to be risk-based, which will reduce the burden of examinations. Further, weekly reporting will allow the agency to identify and respond more quickly to emerging novel and financial stability risks. The weekly reporting will remain confidential because its primary purpose is to inform the OCC's supervision of permitted payment stablecoin issuers and the stablecoin market.
Several commenters provided feedback about the challenges associated with providing reliable and accurate data on a weekly basis on the proposed timelines. One commenter claimed that Form PS-01 effectively establishes a daily reporting obligation across all eight schedules that largely duplicates the GENIUS Act's monthly attestation requirement. The commenter further claimed that collecting and furnishing this data on a daily basis for consolidation into a weekly report creates significant operational demands that, in some cases, may not be possible or may need additional time to verify. The commenter highlighted three categories as particularly problematic to comply with: (i) third-party data; (ii) instrument-level reserve detail; and (iii) operational timing. The commenter further claimed that providing this data in near-real time also minimizes the ability to conduct data validation and reconciliation. The commenter further added that reporting should allow sufficient time to reconcile and evidence reserve balances and payment stablecoins in circulation, rather than require publication of unsupported figures. The commenter also proposed for permitted payment stablecoin issuers in full compliance with the attestation requirements, that the OCC substitute the weekly forms by supplementing the attestation with a randomly selected monthly surprise observation date. The commenter stated that this is a standard that has been successfully used by the New York Department of Financial Services to ensure payment stablecoin issuers maintain identifiable reserves at all times.
Another commenter stated that requiring permitted payment stablecoin issuers to become a routine reporting agent for third-party trading activity is a distinct market surveillance function.
(
printed page 66922)
The commenter added that if the OCC concludes that issuer-based market surveillance is both necessary and authorized, the requirement should be proposed in regulatory text through coordinated notice-and-comment rulemaking. The commenter added that the process should identify the risk each item addresses, the decisions it will inform, the party best positioned to supply it, and a common methodology and accuracy standard. The commenter further added that the Tuesday-to-Wednesday cycle leaves approximately seventeen hours to collect final data from multiple providers, reconcile it, approve it, and submit it. The commenter claimed that preliminary files frequently change after settlement or valuation adjustments, which results in a forced choice between provisional reporting and routine amendments. Two other commenters added that requiring permitted payment stablecoin issuers to file Form PS-01 within less than 24 hours creates a significant recurring operational demand, while also reducing a permitted payment stablecoin issuer's ability to validate data. Another commenter recommended that the OCC eliminate the secondary market pricing line items in Form PS-01 and the OCC obtain real-time pricing data instead of requiring permitted payment stablecoin issuers to report this information.
As discussed in greater detail below, the OCC is revising Form PS-01 and its accompanying schedules to reduce the amount of market data permitted payment stablecoin issuers are required to report. For example, the OCC has removed Items 3 and 4 from proposed Schedule A, which sought data related to trading volume of exchanges. The OCC is eliminating these reporting categories in response to feedback received concerning the operational and validation challenges associated with the collection of third-party data.
In response to these comments concerning the limited amount of time between the close of the reporting period and the reporting deadline, the OCC has elected to maintain the Wednesday, 5:00 p.m. (Eastern) filing deadline for Form PS-01, but revise the reporting period in the proposed instructions for Form PS-01 from “12:00:00 a.m. (Eastern) each Wednesday to 11:59:59 p.m. (Eastern) the following Tuesday” to “12:00:00 a.m. (Eastern) each Tuesday to 11:59:59 p.m. (Eastern) the following Monday.” This change is being implemented to provide permitted payment stablecoin issuers with an additional 24 hours to prepare and submit Form PS-01.
A commenter recommended that the OCC align Form PS-01 reporting with information maintained in a permitted payment stablecoin issuer's books and records as of its ordinary close of business. The commenter observed that the instructions require daily balance items as of 11:59:59 p.m. (Eastern) and daily activity based on transactions occurring from 12:00:00 a.m. through 11:59:59 p.m. (Eastern), including weekends and holidays. The commenter explained that those times may not align with a permitted payment stablecoin issuer's ordinary accounting and posting processes and could require reconstruction of activity beyond its existing books and records. Another commenter added that most blockchain systems currently use a Coordinated Universal Time (or “UTC”) -based reference and shifting to Eastern time zone business hours would add operational complexity without any commensurate supervisory benefit.
The OCC declines to modify the instructions for Form PS-01 to allow permitted payment stablecoin issuers to utilize their preferred close of business. The OCC believes maintaining the 12:00:00 a.m. to 11:59:59 p.m. (Eastern) reporting period promotes consistency and comparability across the reported data. For these reasons, the OCC is maintaining the proposed reporting period. Following implementation of the final rule, the OCC will monitor the reporting process to determine if changes to the reporting instructions are warranted.
